planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in full sun with excellent drainage; Provence is a distinct lavandin cultivar from Grosso, bred for a sweeter, less camphorous fragrance better suited to culinary use.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained to dry soil, spacing plants generously to allow for its broad, mounding size. Provence is a lavandin hybrid (a cross between English lavender and spike lavender) selected for a sweeter, less camphorous fragrance than the widely grown Grosso, making it one of the preferred lavandin cultivars for culinary use, sachets, and light perfumery where a purer floral scent is wanted. Its long, gracefully arching flower spikes hold pale lavender-blue blooms and, like other lavandins, it inherits better heat and humidity tolerance from its spike lavender parentage than pure English lavender, making it a more forgiving choice for Gulf South gardens. Shear spent flower spikes after bloom to prevent the plant from becoming woody and sprawling, and harvest stems just before flowers fully open for the best fragrance and flavor.

common_name: SuperBlue English Lavender (Compact Deep Blue-Purple Lavender)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container-grown transplants in spring in well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; SuperBlue is a compact English lavender selected for deep blue-purple flower color and reliable early bloom.

directions: Plant in full sun with excellent drainage, avoiding heavy clay or consistently moist soils that quickly cause root rot in lavender. SuperBlue bears richly colored, deep blue-purple flower spikes on a compact, tidy plant that blooms earlier and often more heavily than many other English lavender cultivars, with the classic sweet, refined fragrance the species is prized for in culinary and craft use. Its small, dense size fits edging, container growing, and small formal gardens where larger lavender or lavandin types would be out of scale. Trim lightly after the main flush of bloom to maintain a compact shape and encourage a possible second flush, and provide excellent air circulation to reduce fungal disease risk in humid climates.
